metadata.title: From 94.2 Percent to 0.49
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week05/term2-week5-video-content.md (Week 5); judge model names from inbox/week-01/KEYWORD_QA_PIPELINE_DOCS.md; narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27)
metadata.note: Project update. Thesis: same data, different claim — 94.2% raw agreement is moderate agreement (Fleiss' kappa 0.49) after chance correction. Credit: the critique came from the reviewer; the script, the database restore and the paper fixes are Janvi's. Only Professor Brown may be named. WORDING LAW: agreement is never called accuracy; every on-screen number appears in the Week 5 source as written.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about re-measuring our ensemble's agreement with a chance correction. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: Our paper reports 94.2% agreement between three AI judges. How much of that would chance alone give?

beats.role_note: Card '94.2% agreement' with three judge logos (ink); question tag 'chance baseline?' (the reviewer); base-rate chip '45% approved'.
beats.narration_text: Our paper reported 94.2 percent agreement between three AI judges. The reviewer pointed out that a raw percentage means little without a chance baseline. When 45 percent of items get the same tag, judges can agree a lot just by chance.
beats.visual_intent: Card '94.2% agreement' with three judge logos (ink); question tag 'chance baseline?' (the reviewer); base-rate chip '45% approved'.

beats.role_note: Local files: final vote only → Supabase audit table card 'paused' → 'restored'; row count 10,049 intact.
beats.narration_text: To measure it, I needed each model's individual tags, not just the final vote. Those live in our Supabase audit table, which had paused from inactivity. I restored it and confirmed all 10,049 rows were intact.
beats.visual_intent: Local files: final vote only → Supabase audit table card 'paused' → 'restored'; row count 10,049 intact.

show.event: individual tags, not just the final vote

beats.role_note: Script card 'agreement_metrics.py · ~800 lines'; output chips: Fleiss' kappa (three judges) · Cohen's kappa (each pair) · dissenter in 2/1 splits.
beats.narration_text: Then I built a script of about 800 lines to compute Fleiss' kappa across all three judges, Cohen's kappa for each pair, and which model dissents when the vote splits two to one.
beats.visual_intent: Script card 'agreement_metrics.py · ~800 lines'; output chips: Fleiss' kappa (three judges) · Cohen's kappa (each pair) · dissenter in 2/1 splits.

beats.role_note: Two result cards: Keywords · Fleiss' kappa 0.4884 · moderate · N = 8,967 | Acronyms · 0.3847 · fair · N = 885.
beats.narration_text: The result: across 8,967 valid keywords, Fleiss' kappa is 0.49, moderate. For acronyms, it's 0.38, fair.
beats.visual_intent: Two result cards: Keywords · Fleiss' kappa 0.4884 · moderate · N = 8,967 | Acronyms · 0.3847 · fair · N = 885.

beats.role_note: Pairwise bars (Week 1 bar style): Mistral–Claude 0.6559 · Mistral–GPT-4o-mini 0.4251 · GPT-4o-mini–Claude 0.4022; chip 'GPT-4o-mini dissents in 55.8% of splits'.
beats.narration_text: The surprise was in the pairs. Mistral and Claude agree substantially, at 0.66. Both pairs with G P T four o mini sit near 0.4. And in two-to-one splits, G P T four o mini is the dissenter 55.8 percent of the time.
beats.visual_intent: Pairwise bars (Week 1 bar style): Mistral–Claude 0.6559 · Mistral–GPT-4o-mini 0.4251 · GPT-4o-mini–Claude 0.4022; chip 'GPT-4o-mini dissents in 55.8% of splits'.

beats.role_note: Three fix rows, old struck → new: 5.8% → 6.5% (586 / 8,967) · ~74% chance → ~67% · new abstract line 'Accuracy against expert ground truth was not measured.'
beats.narration_text: Writing it up also caught two errors in my own paper. The review share now uses the 8,967 valid items as its denominator, so 586 is 6.5 percent, not 5.8. And I had applied the acronym chance rate, 74 percent, to keywords; the right figure is about 67. I also added one line to the abstract: accuracy against expert ground truth was not measured.
beats.visual_intent: Three fix rows, old struck → new: 5.8% → 6.5% (586 / 8,967) · ~74% chance → ~67% · new abstract line 'Accuracy against expert ground truth was not measured.'

show.event: two errors in my own paper

beats.role_note: '94.2% raw agreement' → '0.49 after chance · moderate'; caption 'same data, different claim'. (Split from Janvi's B07 so the handoff stays a pure composer beat; narration verbatim.)
beats.narration_text: The data didn't change. The claim did: from 94 percent agreement to moderate agreement after chance.
beats.visual_intent: '94.2% raw agreement' → '0.49 after chance · moderate'; caption 'same data, different claim'. (Split from Janvi's B07 so the handoff stays a pure composer beat; narration verbatim.)

beats.narration_text: Your turn: next time you report agreement, compute what chance alone would give, and report both.
